CTGAN is run as a substitute for the paper's own generator in an ablation that asks whether an off-the-shelf tabular synthesiser would do: attack accuracy falls to chance in every case, which is the result the paper uses to argue its logit-conditioned synthesis is what makes the attack work.

paper-research-anchorage-length-grouted-.summary: This conference paper addresses the problem of limited experimental data for determining rebar anchorage length in grouted corrugated duct connections used in prefabricated bridge piers, which causes underfitting in existing empirical equations. The authors preprocess an original small experimental dataset, train a CTGAN model to generate synthetic samples that match its statistical distribution, and use the combined augmented dataset to derive an improved regression equation for anchorage length. CTGAN (the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN) is used as the sole data-augmentation tool underlying the whole empirical programme.
paper-research-anchorage-length-grouted-.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract does not clarify whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly or reimplemented, so integration mechanism (api_user vs port) is unclear. Venue and affiliations not stated in available evidence.

paper-quality-prediction-compressor-blad.summary: This paper proposes a domain generalization-based quality prediction framework for high-precision compressor blade manufacturing, using coordinate measuring machine (CMM) data from historical blades to predict geometric errors on newly designed blades without retraining. The framework is validated on four series of aerospace compressor blades from an industrial manufacturer, achieving low prediction errors across all four blade types. CTGAN (via the SDV-family CTGAN paper) is cited only in a passing reference to deep learning methods needing to meet generalization challenges, with no further engagement in the text.
paper-quality-prediction-compressor-blad.needs: Full text search found no other SDV-family mentions; the citation [15] is a single passing reference in a list of prior deep-learning methods, with no CTGAN usage or discussion elsewhere in the paper.

paper-analysis-research-fraud-detection-.summary: This paper proposes a conditional GAN-based data augmentation method for credit card fraud detection, adding conditional label variables into the generator and discriminator to synthesize realistic fraudulent transactions for training a LightGBM classifier, with PCA and t-SNE used to visualize the synthetic data's coverage. The method is the authors' own conditional GAN implementation rather than a reuse of an existing package. CTGAN is cited in the related-work discussion as prior art that addresses mode collapse and captures complex feature interactions in tabular data, but it is not run in the experiments.

paper-microbiome-ap-crc-2025.summary: Explores whether microbiome profiles can distinguish adenomatous polyps from colorectal cancer, limited by how few sequenced cohorts exist. It names the Synthetic Data Vault Python library explicitly and uses the Gaussian Copula synthesizer, one of the clearer cases in this batch where the library rather than a bare architecture is cited.

paper-bayesian-generation-synthetic-data.summary: This paper introduces and evaluates YABaGen, a tool that uses Bayesian Networks to generate small synthetic datasets that preserve the probability distribution of large source datasets, aiming to reduce computational and storage costs for ML pipelines. The authors assess both the effectiveness (via MMD and classifier accuracy) and efficiency (execution time, memory usage) of models trained on YABaGen-generated data versus the original data. As a state-of-the-art baseline, they run the Synthetic Data Vault tool implementing Gaussian Copula to generate synthetic datasets from the same source data and compare its fidelity, accuracy, and runtime/memory footprint against YABaGen, while CTGAN is only cited in related work and proposed for future benchmarking.
paper-bayesian-generation-synthetic-data.needs: CTGAN is only cited/proposed for future benchmarking, not run; excluded from sdv_component as it was not actually used in experiments.

paper-ctgans-generating-synthetic-traffi.summary: This conference paper explores the use of Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGANs) to generate synthetic traffic matrices for wide-area network research, validating the approach on 167 real traffic matrices from the US Abilene topology and showing high quality scores and preserved statistical/link-load properties. The authors release their experimental code publicly for further use. The CTGAN synthesizer used in the experiments is explicitly the implementation provided by the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, run as the generator underpinning the whole empirical study.
paper-ctgans-generating-synthetic-traffi.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether SDMetrics quality report or conditional sampling were specifically leveraged beyond the base CTGAN model, and no affiliation information is given in the available evidence.

paper-dpt-ddpm-2025.summary: Applies denoising diffusion to tabular generation and compares the result against the GAN generation that preceded it. CTGAN is one of the baselines run, with its output distributions plotted against the real wilt dataset.

paper-defect-prediction-cwdm-optical-202.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning framework for defect prediction in CWDM optical modules, fusing manufacturing process tabular data with optical eye-diagram images, and reports 91.0% accuracy on a real industrial dataset, outperforming single-modal baselines. To address class imbalance in the tabular branch, the authors augment the training data with several techniques including pixel shifting, erasure, and noise injection. CTGAN is trained directly on the tabular dataset for 300 epochs to generate synthetic normal and defective samples that balance the dataset, serving as one of the paper's data augmentation methods.
paper-defect-prediction-cwdm-optical-202.needs: Not stated whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or another implementation was used; assumed api_user given standard naming and epoch-based training description.

paper-fed-ensemble-enhancing-federated-2.summary: This paper proposes Fed-ensemble, a federated-learning framework combining ensemble machine learning models and explainable AI techniques to predict thyroid cancer recurrence while preserving patient data privacy across institutions. To address data scarcity in the underlying 383-sample cohort dataset, the authors augment the data to larger sizes (1500, 5000, 10000 samples) before training. CTGAN is run as the synthetic data generator for this augmentation, with its conditional vector sampling and mode-specific (GMM) preprocessing steps described and used to produce the enlarged, class-imbalanced training datasets.

paper-generative-adversarial-network-ove.summary: This paper addresses class imbalance in three-class botnet detection (spam vs. non-spam vs. normal traffic) by using a GAN-based oversampling method and comparing its performance against SMOTE and no oversampling within a CNN classification pipeline across multiple CTU-13/NCC scenarios. The GAN oversampler achieves more stable accuracy than SMOTE across scenarios, though at the cost of precision in some cases. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library is run to instantiate and train the CTGAN model that generates the synthetic minority-class botnet samples underlying the entire empirical evaluation.
paper-generative-adversarial-network-ove.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly or reimplemented, though the phrasing 'uses CTGAN' suggests direct use.

paper-genetic-algorithm-subset-selection.summary: This paper proposes a genetic-algorithm-based method for selecting high-quality subsets from over-generated synthetic tabular data, aiming to improve data utility for downstream sharing tasks. It is benchmarked on five medical datasets, each synthesized using multiple generative architectures including ARF, CTGAN, TVAE, RTVAE, and Normalizing Flows, showing that GA-selected subsets outperform both the raw synthetic data and random-subset baselines. CTGAN and TVAE are used as two of several generative architectures producing the synthetic datasets that the GA subset-selection method operates on.
paper-genetic-algorithm-subset-selection.needs: Evidence does not confirm whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or a separate implementation; no constructor parameters or library import are shown.

paper-silico-generation-synthetic-cancer.summary: This paper introduces OncoGAN, a generative AI model combining adversarial networks and variational autoencoders to produce realistic synthetic cancer genomes, addressing data-sharing limits caused by privacy concerns in oncology research. The authors validate OncoGAN's synthetic genomes using the DeepTumour classifier and show that augmenting training data with synthetic genomes improves tumor-type prediction accuracy. An SDV-family GAN-based tabular synthesis paper (cited as either TGAN or CTGAN in the available evidence) is referenced only in passing, with no indication it was run as part of OncoGAN's pipeline.

Cannot confirm whether SDV code was run or merely cited as related work.

paper-format-preserving-release-2025.summary: Evaluates re-identification risk across three release strategies, data minimization, anonymization and synthesis, holding the output format constant so the comparison is like for like. CTGAN and TVAE are the generative models in the synthesis arm, so SDV represents synthesis against classical disclosure control.

paper-mitigating-regression-faults-induc.summary: This paper investigates regression faults in deep learning systems caused by feature evolution, identifying redundancy and contribution shift as underlying factors, and proposes FeaProtect, a mitigation approach that outperforms state-of-the-art in-processing and post-processing baselines. As part of a fidelity assurance component for test case generation, the authors note that GAN-based approaches are unsuited to tabular data and instead follow prior work by adapting TVAE to measure semantic similarity between generated and seed test cases.
paper-mitigating-regression-faults-induc.needs: No full text available; unclear whether TVAE was run via the SDV/CTGAN library or reimplemented from scratch, so integration mechanism cannot be confirmed.

paper-use-trajectory-tackling-scarcity-2.summary: This paper proposes using abundant vessel trajectory data, transformed via environmental features, to compensate for scarce fishing-catch datasets, comparing models trained on actual catch reports versus inferred knowledge from trajectories. The case study shows trajectory-derived data can outperform sparse ground-truth records for predicting fishing productivity. CTGAN is cited among the referenced literature, with no visible detail on how or whether it was run.
paper-use-trajectory-tackling-scarcity-2.needs: No full text or citing sentence was available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run, adapted, or merely cited in passing.

paper-pomelo-black-box-feature-2025.summary: This paper introduces POMELO, an extension of the LIME explanation method that uses generative models (normalizing flows and diffusion models) to produce full-input, in-distribution perturbations rather than segment-wise out-of-distribution ones, improving explanation quality for black-box models. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as an example of prior work using Conditional Tabular GANs to enhance LIME's robustness against attacks, with no experiments or code involving it. SDV's CTGAN is cited only as a bibliographic reference to related work, never run.

paper-digital-talent-scholarship-2025.summary: Applies synthesis to Indonesia's Digital Talent Scholarship dataset, which mixes demographic and educational personal information under a national digital transformation programme. CTGAN is the generator, an instance of SDV applied to government administrative data rather than clinical or financial records.

paper-real-time-mouse-protection-2025.summary: This paper proposes a real-time defense for image-based authentication systems in which artificial mouse-cursor data, generated from a user's own historical mouse sequences, is blended with live input to prevent adversaries from distinguishing genuine mouse movements via machine-learning classifiers. The synthetic mouse coordinate and timing data are produced by training a Conditional Tabular GAN on prior sequence data, with epoch counts tuned to minimize an attacker classifier's accuracy. CTGAN, cited to both the NeurIPS paper and the sdv-dev CTGAN GitHub repository, is run directly as the generator that produces all synthetic mouse data underlying the evaluation.

paper-shap-distance-explainability-aware.summary: This paper introduces the SHAP Distance, a metric based on the cosine distance between global SHAP attribution vectors from classifiers trained on real versus synthetic tabular data, aiming to capture semantic fidelity gaps missed by distributional or TSTR-accuracy measures. The authors validate the metric on enterprise, healthcare, and telecom datasets, arguing it reveals feature-importance shifts invisible to standard evaluation toolkits. SDV is cited in the related-work discussion of tabular synthesizers ('Gaussian Copula models have been introduced into the SDV framework'), and SDMetrics is likewise cited as a toolkit that provides standardized but purely statistical quality measures -- neither is run in the experiments.

paper-fabrication-synthetic-promises-tra.summary: This is a sociology-of-science article that applies the sociology of expectations and boundary work to analyze how synthetic data promises are constructed and circulated, drawing on scientific literature, promissory reports, industry webinars, and interviews. It traces transformations in the framing of synthetic data over recent decades and examines boundary work concerning epistemic claims, methodological disputes, and 'fakeness' contestations. SDV's original 2016 paper is cited only as one example of a proliferating body of synthetic data methodology proposals, not engaged with technically.

paper-wind-induced-transmission-line-202.summary: This paper develops a data-driven fragility model for predicting wind-induced transmission line interruptions, tackling the severe class imbalance inherent in rare outage events. It combines a GAN-based synthetic data generation method with an active learning framework for instance selection and SHAP-based sensitivity analysis, achieving notable accuracy gains over conventional methods on unseen and high-uncertainty test cases. CTGAN is cited in connection with the paper's synthetic data generation approach for addressing the extreme data imbalance, though the evidence does not show whether the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation itself was run.
paper-wind-induced-transmission-line-202.needs: Full text needed to determine whether CTGAN was run as a baseline/component or merely cited as related work on GAN-based oversampling for imbalanced data.

paper-case-exploring-synthesis-strategie.summary: This case study from Statistics Netherlands investigates generating synthetic microdata from open-source aggregated (macro) data versus traditional micro-level synthesis, proposing three knowledge scenarios (zero, internal, external) built on a Gaussian-copula-based SYNC method, and evaluating utility and privacy risk via matching attacks. As part of the micro-to-micro baseline comparison, the authors run CTGAN alongside CART to synthesize microdata from real tabular records, comparing rule-violation rates, regression MSE, and residual patterns against their macro-to-micro Gaussian copula approach. CTGAN is used as one of two baseline synthesizers benchmarked against the paper's proposed macro-to-micro synthesis strategy, with the sdv.dev toolkit cited as the source of the CTGAN implementation used.

paper-generative-benchmark-creation-fram.summary: This paper proposes a framework that uses Large Language Models to generate benchmarks for detecting versions of the same data table, addressing the lack of documented, well-labeled versioning benchmarks, and releases VerLLM-v1 as a first instance. In its related-work discussion of prior generative approaches to synthesizing tabular data, it briefly notes that Xu and Veeramachaneni also developed such a method using an RNN-based architecture. TGAN is only cited as prior art in a one-line description, not run or evaluated.
paper-generative-benchmark-creation-fram.needs: TGAN's architecture is mischaracterized as RNN-based in the source text; recorded as the paper's own wording, not corrected.

paper-gtcoder-discrete-prior-fusion-2024.summary: Proposes GTCoder, an autoencoder for tabular synthesis that learns a discrete prior and fuses it with a continuous one, trained with a contrastive objective so that the latent space separates the discrete and continuous modes that mixed-type tables carry. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six deep baselines it is measured against, appearing as rows in both the machine-learning utility tables across six datasets and the likelihood tables on the synthetic grid and ring distributions.

paper-modified-ctgan-plus-features-2024.summary: This paper proposes a portfolio-optimization framework that generates synthetic asset-return scenarios via a modified CTGAN architecture augmented with contextual features (Treasury yield-curve points) and unsupervised clustering of market regimes, feeding the synthetic returns into a CVaR-constrained optimization engine. The authors keep the layers, dimensions and default architecture of the original CTGAN model but add a clustering-derived discrete state column as an extra conditional variable and apply the model to PCA-transformed returns, producing a 'Modified CTGAN-plus-features' synthesizer used as the core generator for a decade-long backtest. CTGAN's conditional-vector and mode-specific normalization design is directly extended into this new state-aware generator, making CTGAN the load-bearing, modified generative engine of the whole study.

paper-secure-publishing-access-service-2.summary: This paper describes the Shareable Data Publishing and Access Service built for the H2020 VITALISE project, which lets Living Labs securely publish anonymised or synthetic versions of sensitive datasets for external researchers to develop and test analytics scripts before remote execution on real data. The architecture, data flows, and validation of the service are presented as enhancements to prior VITALISE work. SDV is cited as one of the tools used to generate synthetic, shareable versions of non-anonymised datasets within the service.
paper-secure-publishing-access-service-2.needs: No full text available; unclear which specific SDV synthesizer or version was used, or whether it was run directly versus described generically as prior art.

paper-ai-surrogate-workloads-2024.summary: Collects more than two million user-analysis job records over 150 days from the workload manager of a large physics computing grid and asks whether a generative model can stand in for that trace, so that data placement and payload allocation policies can be trained without the real submission records. Four tabular generators are trained and compared on per-feature distributions, pairwise feature correlations and distance to the closest record; TVAE, released alongside CTGAN, is one of them, and the paper reports it and CTABGAN+ missing the multi-peaked workload distribution that the diffusion and oversampling baselines track.

paper-evaluation-framework-synthetic-gen.summary: This paper proposes a statistical evaluation framework for ranking synthetic tabular data generators, combining univariate/multivariate quality tests with Friedman and Finner post-hoc statistical analysis, and demonstrates it on two real-world datasets. The framework benchmarks Gaussian Mixture Models against SDV's GaussianCopula, CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN synthesizers, running all of them as evaluation subjects and reporting quality scores and rankings for each. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, GaussianCopula and CopulaGAN models are the core generators evaluated throughout both experimental use cases.

paper-artificial-intelligence-driven-rad.summary: This is a review article surveying artificial intelligence methods used across the radiomics pipeline, including feature selection, segmentation, and model development, covering approaches such as Boruta, random forests, gradient boosting, generative adversarial networks, CNNs, and transformers. It discusses GAN-based approaches for addressing class imbalance in radiomics datasets. CTGAN is cited only as one item in a list of generative-adversarial-network references relevant to data imbalance, with no evidence of it being run or engaged with in the body text.

paper-fedgen-personalized-federated-lear.summary: This paper proposes FedGen, a personalized federated learning framework that generates synthetic data to address client-level class imbalance and improve model customization across heterogeneous clients. It targets non-IID data distributions in federated settings where local classes are underrepresented. The paper cites the CTGAN paper, likely in relation to synthetic tabular data generation techniques used or discussed for imbalance mitigation.

The empirical programme runs none of the SDV-family synthesizers; SDV's original DSAA 2016 paper appears only in the reference list as one of many prior works on synthetic data generation. SDV is only cited, not used, run, or benchmarked in this work.

paper-improving-predictive-maintenance-p.summary: This conference paper addresses predictive maintenance under limited training data by combining feature engineering with a conditional GAN architecture to generate synthetic sensor data, aiming to improve Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation accuracy, reporting a 5% performance gain on turbofan engine degradation data. The authors' proposed method is their own CGAN, not an SDV-family model; the SDV paper and TGAN paper appear only in the reference list among other generative-modeling citations. Neither the Synthetic Data Vault system nor TGAN is described, run, or compared against in the body text.

paper-natural-symbolic-execution-testing.summary: This paper presents NaturalSym, a symbolic execution-based test input generation tool for data-intensive scalable computing (DISC) applications that incorporates user-annotated semantics of program inputs to produce more realistic test data than existing symbolic executors. It is evaluated against BigTest, NaturalFuzz, ChatGPT, and TestMiner on DISC applications and commercial big data benchmarks. SDV is cited in related work as a tool capable of generating natural-looking test cases based on user annotations, but noted as requiring extensive manual configuration and producing an overwhelming volume of test cases, making it less effective for DISC testing.

paper-precious2gpt-combination-multiomic.summary: This paper introduces Precious2GPT, a multimodal architecture combining a Conditional Diffusion model and a decoder-only Multi-omics Pretrained Transformer to generate synthetic transcriptomic and DNA methylation data across species and tissues, building on the authors' earlier Precious1GPT model. It benchmarks its outputs against Conditional GANs, CDiffusion, and MoPT baselines and demonstrates superior age-prediction accuracy and utility in a colorectal cancer target-discovery case study. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on conditional GANs for tabular data, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the text.

paper-synthetic-enhanced-privacy-vae-202.summary: The paper proposes a VAE-GAN based synthetic data generation approach aimed at improving privacy protection while defending against membership inference attacks. It targets tabular data synthesis and evaluates privacy-utility trade-offs of the generated data. The CTGAN paper is cited in this work's reference list, with no further detail available on how it is engaged.

paper-time-dependent-differential-privac.summary: This paper extends the authors' prior TRGAN model for synthetic bank transaction generation with new privacy-preserving mechanisms, including a novel time-dependent differential privacy approach and a stochastic implementation for calibrating the privacy budget. Experiments show improved robustness of transaction generation compared to existing privacy-preserving modifications. CTGAN is cited only as prior work on tabular data generation using conditional GANs, without being run or engaged with beyond a passing mention.

paper-uncertainty-quantification-traffic.summary: This paper proposes a scalable deep-ensemble approach for quantifying data and model uncertainty in spatiotemporal graph neural networks used for traffic forecasting, combining simultaneous quantile regression loss, scalable Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, and Gaussian copula-based generative modeling to construct diverse high-performing model ensembles. The approach is demonstrated on a diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network for short-term traffic forecasting and shown to outperform existing Bayesian and frequentist uncertainty estimation baselines. The SDV package (v0.14.0) is used directly to fit the multivariate Gaussian Copula models that generate new high-performing hyperparameter configurations for the ensemble.

paper-unlocking-biomedical-sharing-struc.summary: This paper presents an in silico pipeline enabling non-technical biomedical scientists to share sensitive cancer datasets by generating synthetic 'digital twin' data through a cloud-based, no-install computational notebook environment, with quantitative, qualitative, and user-experience validation. The synthetic data generation is implemented by running SDV's Tabular Preset (FAST_ML) method with a defined metadata schema to fit, sample, and produce synthetic tabular cancer data, and the outputs are evaluated using SDMetrics' KScomplement score. SDV's Tabular Preset synthesizer and its companion SDMetrics evaluation library are run directly as the generator and evaluator underpinning the paper's entire synthetic data pipeline.

paper-synthesis-improve-length-stay-2024.summary: This paper addresses the problem of predicting hospital length of stay for small, rare-diagnosis patient cohorts in the MIMIC-IV dataset by enriching each cohort's training data with synthetic patient admissions generated from a CTGAN model, then comparing prediction accuracy with and without the synthetic augmentation. The authors fit CTGAN per cohort, use conditional sampling to restrict synthesis to a given ICD code, and evaluate synthetic data fidelity with the SDV library's built-in quality-report score (column shapes and column pair trends). SDV's CTGAN synthesizer and its quality-report/conditional-sampling API are run directly as the core data-generation and evaluation pipeline underlying the paper's entire empirical results.

paper-model-training-method-ddos-2023.summary: This paper studies an ML training method for detecting IoT DDoS attacks in 5G core network traffic, addressing insufficient and imbalanced attack data by building a custom 5G testbed and comparing SMOTE and CTGAN-based data augmentation against a baseline. The authors use CTGAN to synthesize additional attack traffic samples in tabular form and show it reduces the gap between validation and test performance (generalization error), though it lowers raw accuracy/f1 relative to baseline. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run directly via its open-source implementation (cited alongside the original paper) as one of the data augmentation methods evaluated in the study.

paper-responsible-ai-learning-effectiven.summary: Assembles a responsible-AI workflow for judging teaching effectiveness from student data, combining an interpretable decision tree as the global model, SHAP-style explanation, and an adversarial training stage meant to probe rather than fool the model. Synthetic student records at three and five times the size of the real training set are generated and used as the adversarial examples, so the authors can see where the interpretable model's predictive ability breaks down. Two generators produce them, CTGAN and the R package Synthpop, each configured to emit matched volumes and each yielding its own family of adversarially trained models; Synthpop's reach 0.756 accuracy against CTGAN's best of 0.715, though the paper notes CTGAN still supplies the diverse volume needed to probe over- and underfitting. SDV's generator is therefore trained and sampled for one stage of a study whose subject is the explainability framework.

paper-boosting-anomaly-detection-unsuper.summary: This paper proposes TTAD, a test-time augmentation technique for tabular anomaly detection that generates augmented versions of test instances using nearest-neighbor-based methods such as k-Means centroids and SMOTE, combined with a Siamese network for learned distance metrics, showing improved AUC over baseline anomaly detectors across several datasets. The metadata indicates a citation to the CTGAN paper, but no passage referencing SDV, CTGAN, or any related component appears anywhere in the extracted full text, including the reference list. The link to SDV/CTGAN could not be substantiated from the available evidence.

The authors generate all four synthetic datasets using the Synthetic Data Vault library and validate them with statistical tests and ML-efficacy experiments, ultimately identifying CopulaGAN as the best performer. The SDV library's synthesizers (CopulaGAN, CTGAN, TVAE, GaussianCopula) are run directly as the generators under comparison, and its SDMetrics module is used to score synthetic data quality.

paper-pqd-privately-detecting-per-2023.summary: This paper proposes DP-PQD, a differentially-private framework for detecting per-query discrepancies between aggregate statistics computed on private data and on synthetic data produced by any black-box synthetic data generator, with private algorithms for count, sum, and median queries. It is evaluated experimentally on real datasets to show it can reliably flag queries where synthetic data answers deviate from private answers beyond a threshold. SDV (The Synthetic Data Vault) and CTGAN are named in a list of prior synthetic data generators in the related work and reference list, but neither is run or engaged with further in the text.

paper-employing-deep-learning-early-2023.summary: This paper develops an LSTM-based prediction model that uses longitudinal in-home sensor activity data (ORCATECH dataset) to forecast the transition from cognitively healthy status to mild cognitive impairment, with SHAP used to interpret feature contributions such as sleep-related measures. To address class imbalance between cognitively healthy and degenerated subjects, the authors generate synthetic activity time-series data. The SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) Python package is run to synthesize sequential activity data and produce a balanced training dataset for the LSTM model.

CTGAN is cited among the generative models discussed as prior work relevant to materials data generation.

To address sparsely covered regions of color space, the authors attempted data augmentation using the Synthetic Data Vault library's CTGAN and TVAE models, but found the synthetically generated recipes unreliable and instead relied on domain-knowledge-based augmentation. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE models were run directly as an alternative data-augmentation approach and then rejected in favor of a rule-based method.

paper-synthetic-improve-accuracy-human-2.summary: This conference paper compares three synthetic-data generation techniques for augmenting Human Activity Recognition (HAR) training data derived from the mHealth wearable-sensor dataset, evaluating Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and SVM classifiers on real versus synthetic data. Synthetic Data Vault's Probabilistic Autoregressive model (SDV-PAR) and CTGAN are run directly alongside TimeGAN, with CTGAN at 1500 epochs producing the most realistic and highest-accuracy synthetic dataset. SDV's PAR and CTGAN synthesizers are both run as generators in the empirical comparison, forming the core of the study's results.

paper-virtual-wearable-sensor-generation.summary: This Winter Simulation Conference paper investigates DoppelGANger (DGAN), a time-series GAN, for generating subject-specific wearable sensor data derived from the NHANES health survey, evaluating its ability to preserve temporal and multi-dimensional statistical properties. The authors compare DGAN's synthetic attribute distributions against those produced by a second generator using KS-statistic tests across gender, age, and race attributes. CTGAN is run as a comparison benchmark to assess jointly-generated categorical attributes, with its conditional vector, generator loss, and training-by-sampling method described and its output measured against DGAN's.
paper-virtual-wearable-sensor-generation.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or a custom reimplementation, nor the exact role of CTGAN results relative to DoppelGANger's.

paper-ganeraid-realistic-synthetic-patie.summary: This paper proposes GANerAid, an LSTM-based Generative Adversarial Network architecture designed to generate realistic synthetic patient data for clinical trial contexts, aiming to preserve variable correlations and distributions even in small samples. It is released as an open-source Python package. The paper cites the original TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni, 2018) paper, apparently as related prior work in the tabular GAN literature, though the citing sentence itself was not available for review.
paper-ganeraid-realistic-synthetic-patie.needs: Full text and citing sentence not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is merely cited in related work or used as an experimental baseline against GANerAid.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-cr.summary: This paper proposes a WGAN-GP-based generative model, augmented with a predictor and evaluator module, to create synthetic nucleic acid sequences of the cat genome from Illumina sequencing data, aiming to help disease diagnosis and clinical research where genomic data is scarce and sensitive. The authors compare their proposed model against six prior GAN architectures for sequence generation, reporting correlation coefficient, RMSE, and other metrics in a results table. CTGAN and TGAN are run as two of six baseline comparison models against the authors' proposed generator, with CTGAN's performance reported quantitatively in the benchmark table.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-cr.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN/TGAN were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan packages on an encoded representation of nucleic acid sequences, or reimplemented from scratch to fit the sequence-generation task (which is outside CTGAN's native tabular-data design); no library import or reimplementation statement is given.

paper-dequantization-smart-buildings-202.summary: Improves how smart-building sensor tables are transformed before a neural network sees them, pairing variational dequantization for discrete features with mode-specific normalization for continuous ones, and reports the gain on thermal comfort classification. Mode-specific normalization is CTGAN's technique, adopted as one of the paper's two proposed transformations.

paper-gan-effective-membership-inference.summary: This paper proposes KD-GAN, a training framework combining knowledge distillation with generative adversarial networks to defend deep learning models against membership inference attacks, achieving near-random attack success rates while preserving model utility. The framework trains separate GANs for image and tabular/text data, using StyleGAN2-ADA for images and CTGAN for the tabular/text purchase dataset (after clustering to obtain cluster centers). CTGAN is run as one of the two generative models producing synthetic data used within the defence pipeline.
paper-gan-effective-membership-inference.needs: Full text not obtained; unable to confirm whether SDV's packaged CTGAN or an independent reimplementation was used, or further architectural details.

paper-battery-pack-consistency-modeling-.summary: This paper proposes a generative-adversarial-network-based approach to model consistency variations among cells in a battery pack, likely for state estimation or simulation purposes in battery management systems. Full methodological detail is unavailable from the evidence provided. It cites the CTGAN paper (Xu et al., NeurIPS 2019) as related work, with no indication from the metadata of whether CTGAN was actually run.
paper-battery-pack-consistency-modeling-.needs: Full text or abstract needed to determine whether CTGAN was run as a baseline, adopted conceptually, or merely cited in passing; industry/use_case guesses are tentative given only the title and citation list.

paper-wristprint-characterizing-user-ide.summary: This CCS 2021 paper studies how wrist-worn accelerometer data can be used to re-identify users across datasets, using an open-set deep learning formulation trained on a new 10-week, 353-user dataset, finding re-identification risk reaches 96% when a full day of data is shared. In its related-work discussion of privacy protection strategies, it lists synthetic data generation as one general approach, citing SDV and CTGAN only bibliographically without running either.
paper-wristprint-characterizing-user-ide.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so any deeper engagement with SDV/CTGAN elsewhere in the paper cannot be ruled out.

paper-dece-decision-explorer-counterfact.summary: This paper presents DECE, an interactive visualization system for exploring machine learning model decisions using counterfactual explanations, supporting both instance-level and subgroup-level analysis for decision-subjects and model developers. It is a human-computer interaction / explainable AI contribution, not a synthetic-data paper. The TGAN paper on synthesizing tabular data using GANs is cited only in passing, as future-work inspiration for speeding up counterfactual generation via 'smoothing categorical features'.

paper-applications-security-privacy-xxxi.summary: This conference proceedings volume from DBSec 2020 includes a chapter (by Stübs et al.) that evaluates the utility of synthetic data for supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised credit-card-fraud anomaly detection, comparing models trained on real data against data generated by three synthesizers. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is described as building a model using a multivariate Gaussian copula to preserve inter-column correlations, and is run alongside DataSynthesizer and synthpop to produce synthetic training sets whose downstream detection performance is measured. SDV's Gaussian copula synthesizer is one of several generators run as an evaluation subject, with its output directly feeding the anomaly-detection experiments.
paper-applications-security-privacy-xxxi.needs: The metadata title/authors correspond to the whole DBSec 2020 proceedings volume (editors Singhal & Vaidya), but the actual SDV citation occurs in one internal chapter authored by Stübs, Loesch, Mueller, Schupp, and Federrath (identified via page-header and author-index evidence); the chapter's own title was not present in the extracted text.

paper-class-balancing-human-comfort-2019.summary: A poster-abstract paper proposing to use GANs as a pre-processing step to synthesize minority-class samples and rebalance a small thermal-comfort survey dataset for smart-building applications. The authors train their own GAN on a 77-participant thermal comfort dataset and augment underrepresented comfort classes with synthetic samples. TGAN (Tabular-GAN) is cited in related work and described as focusing on marginal feature distributions via a complex generator architecture, but it is not run or used in the experiments.
paper-class-balancing-human-comfort-2019.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was run via the original sdv-dev package, reimplemented, or merely cited as prior art. Integration and importance inferred from abstract/topic alignment with the cited TGAN paper.

preprint-hybrid-machine-learning-synthet.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid synthetic tabular data framework for clinical datasets (breast cancer and cardiology) that combines noise injection, interpolation, GMM sampling, CVAE sampling, and SMOTE via a reinforcement-learning-based dynamic weight selector, followed by post-hoc calibration techniques (moment matching, histogram matching, iterative refinement) to align marginal and joint feature distributions. It reports strong fidelity, privacy, and downstream classifier utility results on UCI Breast Cancer and a Khulna Medical College cardiology cohort. To contextualize performance, the authors benchmark their calibrated hybrid models against four generators available through the Synthetic Data Vault framework -- CTGAN, TVAE, GaussianCopula, and CopulaGAN -- using SDV's quality-report protocol (column shape and pair-trend scores) as evaluation subjects rather than as the proposed method.

preprint-machine-learning-framework-hand.summary: This paper develops a machine-learning framework (MLP, Random Forest, XGBoost) to predict bluebottle (Physalia) beaching events in Eastern Sydney, addressing class imbalance, class overlap, and unreliable absence labels through data augmentation strategies including SMOTE, random undersampling, and a novel 'Synthetic Negative Approach'. The Synthetic Negative Approach uses CT-GAN to generate an entire synthetic negative (absence) class from the positive class distribution, and this CT-GAN-augmented approach combined with Random Forest is found to be the best-performing model overall. CTGAN, cited to the Xu et al. NeurIPS paper for its conditional generator design, is run directly as the data-augmentation generator underpinning the paper's headline predictive results.

preprint-extreme-value-forecasting-relev.summary: This preprint proposes a data augmentation framework for extreme value forecasting in time series, combining deep learning models (Conv-LSTM, BD-LSTM) with GAN-based augmentation and SMOTE, and introduces novel relevance-function-based strategies for incorporating extreme values. The empirical work centers on comparing SMOTE against GAN variants for multistep-ahead prediction accuracy at extremes. CTGAN is cited only in a bibliographic list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs and is never run or engaged with in the body text.

preprint-making-logic-first-class-2025.summary: This paper introduces NetNomos, a multi-stage framework for networking data generation and prediction that mines first-order logic rules from network data and enforces them via collaborative generation between an ML model and an SMT solver, aiming to eliminate rule violations common in generative network models. NetNomos is evaluated against network-specific generators and general-purpose tabular generators across telemetry imputation, traffic forecasting, and synthetic data generation tasks. CTGAN and TVAE (from the CTGAN paper) are run unmodified as two of several general-purpose baseline generators compared against NetNomos on data fidelity and rule-violation metrics.

preprint-robust-detection-synthetic-tabu.summary: This paper proposes a datum-wise transformer architecture for detecting synthetic tabular data under 'in the wild' conditions, where the detector must generalize to previously unseen table schemas and domains. The authors build detection datasets by mixing real rows with synthetic rows produced by several state-of-the-art tabular generators, and introduce a table-adaptation component that improves robustness to schema shift. CTGAN and TVAE are run, alongside TabDDPM and TabSyn, as generators of the synthetic rows the detector must learn to distinguish from real data, with hyperparameters tuned per table.
preprint-robust-detection-synthetic-tabu.needs: Not explicit whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev package or the standalone ctgan/tvae pip package; treated as api_user given named hyperparameter tuning per table.

paper-tabdar-2024.summary: Proposes TABDAR, an auto-regressive transformer for heterogeneous tabular data in which continuous columns are handled by a nested diffusion head and column order is randomized through masked training, so one model serves unconditional generation, arbitrary conditional generation and imputation. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the ten compared generators, run from the TabSyn code base and reported on marginal and joint fidelity, alpha-precision, beta-recall, a classifier two-sample test and downstream machine learning efficacy across ten datasets.

preprint-distributionally-adversarially-.summary: This paper studies distributionally and adversarially robust logistic regression, proposing 'Inter-ARO', which tightens the Wasserstein ambiguity set of a distributionally robust adversarial training problem by intersecting it with a second ambiguity set built from an auxiliary dataset, yielding a tractable convex reformulation and efficient algorithms. In experiments on UCI datasets, the authors split off a portion of each dataset and fit the SDV package's Gaussian Copula synthesizer on it to generate the auxiliary synthetic data used to build this second ambiguity set. SDV's Gaussian Copula model is run directly as the generator producing the auxiliary data underlying the paper's core empirical evaluation.

paper-tabebm-2024.summary: Fits a separate energy-based model per class, using a pretrained in-context classifier as the surrogate so no generator training is needed, and argues that estimating each class distribution on its own avoids the degradation joint-distribution generators show on very small tables; augmentation then improves downstream accuracy where the compared generators reduce it. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the eight benchmark generators, run at default settings from their Synthcity implementations across accuracy, fidelity and privacy comparisons.

preprint-weakly-augmented-variational-au.summary: This work proposes a VAE-based framework for time series anomaly detection that combines self-supervised learning with augmented latent representations, introducing a practical implementation called WAVAE that improves robustness to normal data and sensitivity to anomalies. Experiments on five public synthetic and real datasets show improved ROC-AUC and PR-AUC over state-of-the-art baselines. CTGAN is only cited in passing, in a reference-list mention among examples of deep generative models used for tabular data.

preprint-centric-perspectives-challenges.summary: This is a survey/position paper that maps out data-centric AI (DCAI) as a field, organizing techniques into training data development, inference data development, and data maintenance, and outlining open challenges for the research community. It does not run any experiments itself but cites prior work exemplifying each technique category. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of the 'data synthesis' technique that fabricates data following the original distribution.
preprint-centric-perspectives-challenges.needs: The reference numbering in the visible bibliography excerpt does not clearly match [6] to CTGAN; the exact citation could not be directly verified from the extracted reference list.

preprint-synthetic-generation-techniques.summary: This preprint compares TVAE, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN as synthetic data generators for augmenting a small acoustic-feature dataset used to train machine-learning classifiers that detect Parkinson's disease from speech. The three techniques are run to produce synthetic samples, evaluated with a quality score, and the resulting datasets are used to train several classifiers (RandomForest, ExtraTrees, etc.) whose performance is compared across generators. CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN, all part of the SDV library (CopulaGAN being SDV-exclusive), are run directly as the generators whose outputs form the entire empirical comparison in the paper.
preprint-synthetic-generation-techniques.needs: No affiliation information given in the evidence for the sole author.

preprint-triage-characterizing-auditing-.summary: This NeurIPS 2023 paper introduces TRIAGE, a model-agnostic data characterization framework for regression tasks that scores training samples as under-, over-, or well-estimated using conformal predictive distributions, enabling data sculpting, dataset selection, and feature acquisition. As one experiment, the authors simulate two competing synthetic-data vendors by generating training data with CTGAN and TVAE (citing their implementations from github.com/sdv-dev/SDV) and use TRIAGE to compare which vendor's synthetic data yields better downstream regression performance. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE are run as evaluation subjects in this synthetic-data-vendor scenario, not as the paper's core method.

paper-dp-cgans-correlation-2022.summary: Proposes DP-CGANS, a conditional GAN for tabular data whose conditional vector is built to preserve correlations between variables rather than only marginal distributions, trained under differential privacy so that the synthetic records carry a stated privacy cost. Its continuous-column encoder is the mode-specific normalization proposed in the CTGAN paper, adopted directly; CTGAN is one of the three GAN frameworks it is measured against; and the whole comparison is run inside SDGym, the SDV project's benchmarking suite, which supplies the utility and privacy metrics reported.

preprint-copula-flows-synthetic-generati.summary: This paper proposes a probabilistic synthetic-data generator based on copula theory, using normalising flows to separately model univariate marginals and the multivariate copula density, and benchmarks the approach on simulated and real datasets for both density estimation and downstream ML utility. In related work it identifies the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) project as closely aligned in spirit, noting SDV learns marginals via a Gaussian mixture model and the joint dependency via a Gaussian copula, and in its main experiments it compares against CTGAN and TVAE as baseline generators. SDV is cited descriptively for its Gaussian-copula approach while CTGAN and TVAE are run as comparison baselines that the proposed copula-flow method outperforms.

preprint-pearl-synthesis-private-embeddi.summary: This paper proposes PEARL, a differentially private data synthesis framework that sanitizes sensitive data once via a private embedding (based on the characteristic function) and then trains a generative model implicitly through an adversarial reconstruction objective, avoiding the repeated privacy-budget costs of DP-SGD-style training. It is evaluated against DP-MERF and other DP generative baselines on tabular and image datasets, showing better utility at comparable privacy levels. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only in the related-work/reference discussion of prior deep generative approaches to tabular data synthesis, without being run or compared in the experiments shown.
preprint-pearl-synthesis-private-embeddi.needs: Full text excerpts do not show CTGAN discussed or benchmarked in the body beyond the bibliography; cannot confirm whether a later section (not shown) engages with it more directly.

preprint-synthetic-privacy-mirage-2020.summary: This paper introduces an evaluation framework for quantifying the privacy gain of publishing synthetic data versus raw data, measuring re-identification and attribute disclosure risks across generative models ranging from simple histograms to differentially private GANs. It finds synthetic data offers little privacy protection even under weak adversarial assumptions, challenging claims that synthetic data is inherently privacy-preserving. CTGAN is discussed as an example generative model, with its mode-specific normalisation of tabular attributes described as a technique for approximating complex distributions through GANs.
preprint-synthetic-privacy-mirage-2020.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN is actually run as one of the generative models empirically evaluated in the privacy framework or only described in related-work discussion.

preprint-transfer-learning-thermal-comfo.summary: This paper proposes a transfer learning-based multilayer perceptron model (TL-MLP-C*) that leverages sensor data from multiple cities within the same climate zone to address data scarcity in thermal comfort prediction, evaluated on ASHRAE RP-884, the Scales Project, and Medium US Office datasets. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is cited only in the reference list and does not appear anywhere in the body text, indicating no engagement with the method.

repo-synthetic-data-pybcn.summary: Talk material for a Python Barcelona session on generating synthetic data for AI digital twins, with a worked notebook and a matching exercise notebook. SDV is the whole of the hands-on part: both notebooks import `CTGANSynthesizer`, `CopulaGANSynthesizer` and `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` from their `sdv.single_table` submodules, describe the table with `SingleTableMetadata`, fit and sample, then score with SDMetrics' `QualityReport` and `get_column_plot`. SDV's synthesizers and SDMetrics are run end to end as the session's teaching material.
